idea: Keep a conventional high-temperature Si 1T1C array (1-beta-class cell with a short capacitor), finish it including its capacitor, cap it with oxide, and transfer a ~50 nm single-crystal Si layer on top by Smart Cut. Build the sense amplifiers, sub-wordline drivers and decoders in that layer with CEA-Leti-style 400-500 C n&p CMOS. Connect each 64-128-cell bitline segment to its sense amp with a lithographically aligned via (~100-200 nm, overlay ~5-10 nm) instead of a hybrid-bond pad (>=300-400 nm pitch, ~50-100 nm overlay). This delivers A1 white space 1 (one sense amp per short bitline) at 1-beta pitch without the bond-pitch wall and without the second periphery wafer of bonded periphery-under-cell.
why: Capacitor 1.3 um -> 226-376 nm (AR 62 -> 11-18) with no mux; one wafer instead of two (vs bonded PUC); array efficiency ~0.51 -> ~0.7 (1.37x density).

title: Vertical oxide semi-floating-gate 1T1D gain cell (4F2, capacitor-less, stackable)
idea: A vertical ALD In2O3/IGZO channel pillar is wrapped by a metal floating gate (FG), which is wrapped in turn by a control-gate wordline. A Schottky or MIS diode (Pt/IGZO, p-NiO/IGZO heterojunction, or a thin Al2O3 tunnel diode) links the FG to the drain/bitline at the pillar top. Write: the wordline couples the FG below the bitline, the diode forward-biases and the FG charges to the bitline level. Hold: raise the wordline so the diode is reverse-biased. Read: the FG charge sets the channel current, non-destructively. The reverse current of the diode sets retention, and the cell fits in the footprint of one vertical transistor. Fudan's Si SFG (Science 2013) showed ns writes at <2 V, but its embedded TFET/diode made it large; oxide BEOL lets the diode sit vertically on top.
why: 2.5x per-tier density vs 10F2 2T0C: at F = 20 nm, b x N for 1b parity falls from 3.7 to 1.5; at F = 40 nm (single-exposure ArF, no EUV) from 14.9 to 6.0 (e.g., 2 bits x 3 tiers).

title: Fluorine-free carbon mold for capacitor holes and sacrificial 3D tiers
idea: Replace the SiO2 capacitor mold with a 1.3-2.5 um PECVD amorphous-carbon film (the 3D-NAND hardmask material) capped by a thin SiN or Al2O3 support lattice. Holes are etched anisotropically in O2/COS or H2/N2 plasma (sulfur or nitrogen sidewall passivation, no fluorine). ALD electrode and dielectric (or oxide channel) fill the holes; the carbon is then burned out by O2 or removed by H2 plasma, leaving free-standing, lattice-supported structures. In 3D stacks, carbon replaces SiN as the sacrificial tier: a low-pressure thermal O2 burn is reaction-limited, so the lateral recess is uniform from top to bottom of the stack, and the product is CO2.
why: Eliminates fluorocarbon gas from the capacitor/channel-hole modules (~5.6e13 HAR holes per wafer at 1-beta) and makes 3D lateral recess a thermal, reaction-limited step; the mold leaves ~0.6 g CO2/wafer instead of PFAS-class by-products.

title: ASD self-aligned landing pads and top contacts
idea: After the contact plugs are exposed in dielectric, Mo (or W) is deposited by area-selective ALD/CVD that nucleates only on metal or semiconductor surfaces, with small-molecule or SAM inhibitors on the dielectric and periodic atomic-layer-etch 'defect clean' cycles to remove stray nuclei. The pad grows a controlled height and mushroom width, self-aligned to its plug, so the landing-pad litho/etch step (patterned with EUV or multipatterning at leading nodes [UNVERIFIED-PK]) is not needed. The same approach caps vertical oxide channels in 4F2 VCT and gain-cell arrays.
why: -1 to -2 critical litho layers (~$165-330/wafer if EUV-patterned; 3.8-7.7% of a 1c wafer) and fewer fluorocarbon etches; Mo replaces WF6-based W.

title: Ge-free, NAND-line 3D oxide gain cell (oxide/nitride mold + channel replacement)
idea: Deposit 16-64 SiO2/SiN pairs by PECVD (standard NAND tools). One HAR hole/slit etch exposes all tiers; SiN is removed with hot phosphoric acid and replaced in every tier by ALD IGZO/ZTO horizontal channels (Kioxia's 3D OCTRAM SiN->InGaZnO replacement) plus recessed W/Mo gate and storage-node fills. Vertical wordline pillars gate the write transistors through all tiers (IMECAS dual-gate vertical-WL 2T0C); each storage node is a metal island that gates the tier's read transistor, so no lateral capacitor is needed. 2-3 bits/cell with write-verify multiplies the tier count.
why: 1.1-3.4x 1-beta density at F=40 nm with 16 tiers (1-3 bits), 6.8x at 32 tiers x 3 bits, with no EUV, no Ge and no epitaxy; runs on 3D-NAND tool sets.

title: Etch-compensated graded tier stack: uniform lateral recess by composition grading
idea: 3D DRAM sets each cell's channel and capacitor length by a lateral recess from a vertical hole or slit, and Lam notes that recess sizes vary along the stack because the etchant depletes with depth. Instead of fighting that with chemistry, pre-compensate at deposition: ramp each tier's sacrificial composition with depth (Ge fraction in SiGe, Si/N ratio and hydrogen content in SiN, or boron level in B3-06 layers) so the intrinsic etch rate rises where etchant supply falls. Calibrate the profile once per stack recipe from per-tier TEM; the only tool knob is a gas-flow ramp. Finish with a few tens of lateral atomic-layer-etch cycles to trim the last nanometres uniformly.
why: Recess spread +-12.5% -> +-2.5%: 8% smaller cell pitch along the recess and 11% higher worst-case Cs at 64 tiers; or ~2x taller deck (~130 vs ~66 tiers) per hole etch at equal uniformity, halving decks and HAR etches.

title: Significance-split memory: gold-grade sign/exponent, sand-grade mantissa
idea: The memory controller (GPU or HBM base die) splits tagged tensors (weights, KV, activations) into bit-plane groups placed in different banks, so both are fetched in parallel. Sign and exponent are Huffman-coded to ~3 b (entropy ~2.6 b of 8) and stored in normal rows with ECC and standard refresh. The 7 mantissa planes go to 'approximate' banks with four relaxations: no ECC parity, refresh at ~1 s (raw BER ~1e-5), an optional separate lower VARY rail (~0.75 V), and lower-swing I/O lanes run at BER ~1e-6. Dies or subarrays that fail exact screening (weak cells, high-offset SAs) are binned for mantissa duty instead of scrapped. Ordinary data stays exact; a page-attribute bit selects the mode.
why: For BF16 tensors: x1.58 capacity per DRAM bit (18 -> 11.4 cells per value incl. ECC), x3.7 less refresh energy per value, ~x2 less array energy and ~x2.8 less I/O driver energy on mantissa planes. FP8 x1.41; FP4 x1.18: the lever shrinks as formats narrow.

title: Self-assembled tier stack: parallel block-copolymer lamellae + sequential infiltration synthesis [SPECULATIVE]
idea: A lamella-forming BCP (L0 25-40 nm) with preferential wetting on both interfaces orders parallel to the substrate after annealing, giving 25-80 alternating layers in a 1-2 um film. Sequential infiltration synthesis (TMA/H2O) converts the PMMA layers into AlOx sheets; the PS layers remain as sacrificial carbon tiers (removed later by oxidation, as in B2-10). A single hole etch then opens all tiers; lateral recess and ALD oxide-channel/gate fills proceed as in B2-09. Tier thickness is set by polymer molecular weight rather than deposition time.
why: 25-80 tiers per coat vs one PECVD pair per tier: tier-formation tool time ~10-50x lower [ESTIMATE]; no SiN/SiGe stack.

title: Negative-capacitance bitline: electrophysiology's capacitance neutralisation applied to the DRAM sense path
idea: A small amplifier per bitline (or a pre-phase folded into the existing sense amplifier) senses the bitline and drives a feedback capacitor Cf with gain A > 1. That injects a current equal to -Cn*dV/dt, with Cn = (A-1)*Cf. For the 1-2 ns of charge sharing, the bitline's effective capacitance becomes Cbl - Cn; then the neutraliser switches off and the normal latch fires. At Cn/Cbl ~0.7 the cell can shrink 3.3x for the same signal. Amplifier offset is auto-zeroed during precharge.
why: Capacitor height falls from 1.3 um to ~260 nm (Cs 5.4 to 1.1 fF) at Cn/Cbl = 0.7, with the same 512-cell bitline. Cost: ~5-8% more periphery area (one amplifier per bitline) and no change to the array architecture.

title: Charge-transfer pre-sense on a long bitline: sub-fF cells without shortening the bitline
idea: Conventional sensing divides the cell charge by Cs + Cbl (35 fF), so only ~7 mV survives from a 0.5 fF cell. In charge-transfer pre-sensing (Arimoto/Mitsubishi lineage) the bitline is precharged through its own transfer gate, which therefore self-biases at its own threshold and cancels Vt mismatch. When the cell dumps charge, the bitline moves a few mV, the transfer gate conducts in subthreshold, and the charge flows onto a small sense node. Gain = Cbl/C_sn. The twist is pairing this with an IGZO access device (1 aA), so a 0.3-0.5 fF cell still retains 45-75 s, and using offset-cancelled latches. The capacitor becomes a ~120 nm stub (AR ~6) or even the gate-plus-junction capacitance of a vertical channel.
why: 10x smaller storage capacitor (5.4 -> 0.5 fF; pillar 1,300 -> ~120 nm) at today's 512-cell bitline. Signal on the sense node 155 mV vs 7.5 mV conventional.

title: Adiabatic refresh: recycle bitline and wordline charge with stepwise tanks or piezo-MEMS resonators
idea: During refresh (and optionally background activates), the VARY and VPP rails feeding a bank are ramped rather than fixed. The ramp comes from either (a) N-step tank-capacitor banks (stepwise charging) or (b) a resonant LC whose inductor is a compact AlN piezoelectric MEMS resonator or a package inductor, as in adiabatic or reversible logic. The sense amplifier makes its regenerative decision with a small non-adiabatic kick, then the bitline swing to VARY or 0 follows the ramped rails, and precharge returns charge to the tanks instead of shorting it. Wordlines (3 V, pumped at ~45% efficiency) are ramped the same way. No cell change is needed.
why: Refresh energy per bit falls 2.4-3.2x (refresh-only 29.8 fJ to ~9-13 fJ), from ~12 mW to ~4 mW per 16Gb die, with no new cell and no new materials.

title: Vertical oxide CCD string: transistor-less 3D charge-shift memory
idea: Etch one high-aspect-ratio hole through 128-256 alternating W/Mo and SiO2 word planes (the same module as 3D NAND), and line it with a thin gate oxide and an ALD IGZO/IGO channel. Clock planes in 4 phases (2 gates per bit): each bit is a packet of ~1,000-5,000 electrons in an accumulation well. Si CCDs lose stored charge to thermal generation (dark current); wide-gap IGZO generates essentially no carriers, so packets hold, limited only by inter-well barriers and gate leakage. Reading shifts packets out of the top of the string into a charge-transfer sense amp (B1-04) on bonded periphery, and data recirculates to the bottom: a delay-line memory with 32-64-bit strings and thousands of parallel holes per line access. Planes are segmented into small blocks to keep plane RC at ~1 ns per phase.
why: 4.2-8.3x 1b density (1.85-3.7 Gb/mm2 at 128-256 planes) with zero per-bit devices; streaming read energy 17-67 fJ/bit; but access is serial (32-128 ns worst-case to a given bit).

title: NEMS relay access switch: zero-GIDL DRAM cell
idea: A vertical TiN/W cantilever or clamped beam over each storage node is pulled in by the wordline electrode, closing a contact between bitline and capacitor; open, an air or vacuum gap isolates the node. Leakage then is only the capacitor dielectric's own (~1e-8-1e-7 A/cm2). Switching is abrupt (effectively 0 mV/dec), so the wordline needs only the pull-in voltage (~1 V) with no charge pump. A 100-200 nm beam resonates at 0.4-1.2 GHz, giving ~0.5-1.5 ns mechanical switching. Contacts switch only fC of charge at uA levels, far gentler than RF-MEMS hot switching.
why: Refresh 150-1,500x less frequent (10-100 s retention with today's capacitor); wordline energy ~0.06x (1 V unpumped vs 2.9 V pumped); hammer-immune by construction.

title: Main memory inside the logic die's own metal stack (monolithic BEOL oxide gain cells)
idea: After the logic metal stack is complete (TSMC has already embedded an oxide-semiconductor-selector memory fully in BEOL above advanced logic), deposit 8-16 tiers of vertical IGZO/ZTO 2T0C cells with 3 bits/cell write-verify, local complementary-oxide sensing (B2-08) and short vias down to SRAM-buffered memory controllers. Oxide cells retain >200 s at 95 C, so they tolerate sitting on hot logic. On backside-power logic, the frontside BEOL is less congested. Capacity is the target, not cache: an 800 mm2 die area carries 76-152 GB.
why: 76-152 GB over an 800 mm2 die (3 b x 8-16 tiers at F=40 nm, no EUV); interface energy 3.5 -> ~0.2 pJ/bit, saving 211-422 W per accelerator at 8-16 TB/s; zero extra wafers; added cost ~$0.87/GB at $500 per tier per wafer and 80% yield.

title: 2-bit/cell 1T1C on an oxide access device
idea: Write one of four levels (0, 1/3, 2/3, 1 x VARY) through a vertical IGZO access transistor (OCTRAM/Samsung VCT style). Read by successive approximation: charge-share onto a short bitline, decide the MSB against a mid reference, then the LSB against a reference chosen by the MSB (or a time-domain ramp), then restore all four levels. A silicon cell cannot do this, because its 13 fA tail leaks a full level in milliseconds. At 1 aA the droop is 0.18 mV/s, so a 15 mV level budget lasts ~80 s. Combine with 128-cell bitlines (bonded periphery) or charge-transfer pre-sense (B1-04) for margin.
why: 2x bits per cell -> 1.8-2.8x die density at the same F, depending on array efficiency (0.89-1.23 Gb/mm2 vs 0.447), with no new lithography.

title: Compact-then-sleep: compress, pack, partial-array self-refresh
idea: The memory controller (phone SoC or server CXL controller) carries a hardware compaction engine. When it detects idle, it walks live pages, LZ4-compresses them (2-3x is typical for Marvell-class engines), packs them into the lowest segments and updates a remap table. It then issues partial-array self-refresh (PASR) masks that leave the vacated segments unrefreshed. Combined with B4-02's ECC-stretched self-refresh interval (1 s at 85 C, longer when cool). On wake, pages decompress on first touch (us-scale, like a minor fault) or eagerly in the background.
why: Idle refresh power /2-3 from compaction alone, and /32-48 with ECC-stretched self-refresh: a 64 GB RDIMM drops from 0.49 W to 10-15 mW.
